skill_title: Explain inflation's effect on buying power and salaries
notes: 20-item bank, Grade 12 only. CAPS mix: 10 L3 / 10 L4. Argue with calculations: real vs nominal increases. Justify salary requests using inflation.

stimulus.inline: If salary rises by less than inflation, REAL purchasing power falls.

items.question: Salary rose 5% but inflation was 8%. What was the change in real purchasing power?

stimulus.inline: Salary R20 000 today, 6% inflation, no raise.

items.question: Calculate REAL salary in 1 year (today's-Rand equivalent).

stimulus.inline: Salary R15 000 rose to R15 750.

items.question: Calculate the nominal % increase.

stimulus.inline: Nominal raise 5%, inflation 6%.

items.question: Calculate approximate real % change.

stimulus.inline: Rent rose 7%, salary 5%. Argue the case for raise of 10%.

items.question: What is the real % change in salary (salary 5% rise, inflation 7%)?

stimulus.inline: Purchasing power calculation: 1 / (1 + i).

items.question: With 6% inflation, what fraction of original purchasing power do you have after 1 year?
workingSteps: 1 ÷ 1,06 ≈ 0,9434 ≈ 0,94 (you have 94% of last year's buying power).

stimulus.inline: Compare salaries adjusted for inflation.

items.question: Worker A's salary rose from R20 000 to R22 000 (10% rise). Inflation was 8%. Did real income grow?
options: No — real income stayed the same.

stimulus.inline: Adjust prices for inflation when comparing across years.

items.question: Item cost R50 in 2020; in 2025 it costs R75. Was the price increase ABOVE or BELOW inflation if 5-year inflation was 35% cumulative?
workingSteps: Item price grew faster than inflation → real price rose.

stimulus.inline: Pensioner has R5 000/month pension, no annual adjustment. 5 years of 6% inflation.

items.question: Calculate the real value of the pension in 5 years' time (in today's Rand). Round to nearest Rand.

Compare two raise scenarios. Salary R20 000 today.

- Plan A: +R1 000 fixed each year.
- Plan B: +6% each year.

items.question: After 5 years (compound), what is each salary? Round to nearest Rand.

stimulus.inline: From the previous example.

items.question: Which plan is better after 5 years if inflation is 6%?
options: Plan B — matches inflation, preserving real value.
items.expectedAnswer: Plan B — matches inflation, preserving real value.
workingSteps: Plan A loses to inflation; Plan B exactly matches inflation each year, so real income stays flat.

items.question: Over 10 years at 7% inflation, what fraction of today's purchasing power remains? Round to 2 dp.

items.question: Total nominal cost over 20 years?

stimulus.inline: Bread R20 today, R26 in 5 years. Inflation 6%/year.

items.question: Is the bread price keeping up with inflation, exceeding it, or below?
workingSteps: Actual R26 < R26,76 → bread rose slightly below inflation.

stimulus.inline: Justify a salary increase request. Salary R18 000, asking for 9% in a 6% inflation environment.

items.question: What is the real % gain if granted?

stimulus.inline: A learner says: 'Saving R1 000 today in a 0% interest account is the same as having R1 000 in 5 years.' Critique.

items.question: Is the learner correct?
options: No — inflation makes the R1 000 less valuable in 5 years (it buys less).
items.expectedAnswer: No — inflation makes the R1 000 less valuable in 5 years (it buys less).
workingSteps: Inflation reduces purchasing power. R1 000 nominal in 5 years buys less than R1 000 today.

stimulus.inline: Income tax brackets adjust below inflation (bracket creep). Suppose tax brackets rise by 4% but income rises by 6%.

items.question: Does the worker pay more or less of their income as tax?
options: Less — the brackets are higher so they pay less.
More — incomes rise faster than the brackets, pushing income into higher brackets (bracket creep).
items.expectedAnswer: More — incomes rise faster than the brackets, pushing income into higher brackets (bracket creep).
workingSteps: When bracket thresholds rise less than wages, real tax burden rises (bracket creep).

_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_REAL_VS_NOMINAL: Confuses nominal Rand growth with real (inflation-adjusted) value.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PERCENT_CHANGE_DIVISOR: Divides change by the wrong base.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_PERCENT_INCREASE: Doesn't apply (1 + r) to find new value.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_COMPOUND_AS_SIMPLE: Treats compound inflation as simple addition.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_POWER_OF_FACTOR: Doesn't raise (1 + i) to the power n.
_error_signal_vocabulary.ERR_MARGINAL_RATE: Confuses marginal and average tax rates.
